summary: FireSense turns NASA FIRMS hotspot exports into an auditable burning activity calendar. Users explore global 2026 observations and U.S. historical records, select geographic bounds and dates, compare MODIS with VIIRS, and inspect an experimental sensor adjustment evaluated on separate years. Every view distinguishes observations from inference and standard archives from provisional near-real-time data.
details: FireSense is a local, auditable atlas of NASA FIRMS satellite hotspot detections that helps people explore when and where heat was observed over time on a map, month-by-month calendar, and seasonal profile - keeping MODIS and VIIRS, and standard archive vs near-real-time, clearly separate so counts stay honest (detections, not unique fires). Built with Node.js 24, HTML/CSS, and SQLite (~28.8 million reconciled observations), plus an offline demo and GitHub Pages app, it benefits non-experts by making seasons readable (for example, California January 2025 was almost four times a typical January’s detections by median) while an experimental held-out MODIS→VIIRS monthly mapping - trained 2013–2021, selected 2022, calibrated 2023, tested only on 2024–2025 - beat a fitted ratio by about 12.9% MAE on 72 region-months in three U.S. boxes. The intended impact is clearer public understanding of what satellites can and cannot prove; the creative choice is pairing an explorable calendar with chronological evaluation instead of silently fusing sensors or claiming forecasts; and the team prioritized scientific honesty, provenance, usability, reproducibility, and explicit limits such as incomplete pre-2026 global coverage and no early-warning claims.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS - Fire Information for Resource Management System
